messages:
incident-bot: :warning: INCIDENT 1943216789 - increased error rate and latency observed on inference-router -> /v1/embeddings/generate (region: us-east-1). 5xxs and 429s spiking since 1943216700. Paging oncall.
sara: acked. investigating now. seeing lots of large batch requests from a handful of customers.
kevin: on the metrics dashboard I can see request size distribution jumped — median tokens per request up 6x over baseline. KV cache growth and GPU memory spikes on embedding workers. likely batching blowup + some very large vectors.
liam: can we do a quick per-route throttle to stop the tail? prefer to avoid whole-service disable. suggest: reduce global embeddings QPS, apply per-customer cap for top offenders, and temporarily lower max_batch_size for embeddings workers.
abby: prepping mitigation. I'll push targeted rate limits and per-customer quotas via control plane now. Will post commands and confirmation.
abby: running:
```
ctl quota update --route /v1/embeddings/generate --global-rps 200 --per-customer-rps 5 --max-burst 20 --expires 10m
ctl route-config set --route /v1/embeddings/generate --max-batch-size 8 --expires 10m
ctl throttle add --route /v1/rerank --global-rps 50 --per-customer-rps 2 --expires 10m
```
abby: command outputs: SUCCESS for embeddings limits, SUCCESS for batch-size change, SUCCESS for rerank throttle. Changes propagated to us-east-1 in ~12s. :white_check_mark:
sara: seeing immediate drop in 5xxs and GPU mem pressure. latency on embeddings still a bit higher than baseline but trending down.
kevin: note — chat endpoints (/v1/chat) are fine. we intentionally left chat quotas unchanged because of high-productivity customers hitting chat. we should add route-specific alerts to detect collateral impact.
support-bot: Notifying top 20 affected customers with temporary mitigation message template. Ticket created: INC-1943216789. Template: "We're throttling embeddings/rerank traffic briefly to protect availability; no action needed unless you require higher throughput — please reply."
liam: For customers hitting the per-customer cap, we can offer scheduled quota bump via support if they have reserved capacity. For now, tracks in incident ticket.
abby: adding short-lived rule to route routing to fallback smaller embedding model for large requests:
```
ctl model-route add --route /v1/embeddings/generate --condition "tokens>2048" --fallback-model "embedding-lite-v1" --expires 10m
```
Result: ACCEPTED, routing rule active.
sara: observed tail requests being routed to embedding-lite-v1, memory pressure stabilized. 429s reduced by ~85% in last 3m.
kevin: good. can we also apply a soft quota for rerank (seen big batch scoring spikes from a couple of third-parties)? we applied some throttle but let's note specific offending customer IDs: cust_112, cust_998.
abby: added customer-scoped rule:
```
ctl quota set --route /v1/rerank --customer cust_112,cust_998 --rps 1 --expires 30m
```
SUCCESS. will monitor.
sara: preparing handoff notes in thread: mitigation implemented = per-route throttles (embeddings global 200rps, per-customer 5rps), rerank throttle + customer-specific caps, fallback model for oversized embeddings, batch-size cap reduced. Observed impact: 5xxs down 90%, 429s down 60%, latency trending to baseline. Next steps: keep rules for 30m then reevaluate; support to contact affected customers; postmortem owner: kevin.
next-oncall: taking the rest of the incident. please add any outstanding runbook links and escalate if we see another spike. I have console access to revert rules if needed. leaving a note in PagerDuty that this is in mitigation state.
support-bot: Updated ticket INC-1943216789 with mitigation summary + list of affected customers. Notifying sales for any enterprise customers impacted.
abby: saved rollback commands in case we need to revert quickly:
```
ctl quota delete --id <rule-id>  # revert per-route/per-customer caps
ctl route-config set --route /v1/embeddings/generate --max-batch-size 128
ctl model-route remove --route /v1/embeddings/generate --id <rule-id>
```
kevin: please include the exact rule ids in the incident doc. also will kick off a follow-up to add automatic small-request path for embeddings to avoid future large-batch memory spikes.
next-oncall: acknowledged. I'll monitor for 30m and then either clear the incident or escalate to oncall rotation. setting a 10m alert window for any >10% error-rate regression.
incident-bot: INCIDENT 1943216789 - mitigation in place. status: partial-service-stable. monitor window started.
